common_name: Princess Ariane Alstroemeria (Yellow Peruvian Lily with Rosy-Pink Blotched Petal Tips)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots in spring in fertile, moist but well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade; Princess Ariane is a compact selection from the Princess Lily series.

directions: Princess Ariane is a compact, clump-forming member of the Princess Lily series, carrying yellow flowers with a deep rosy-pink blotch at the petal tips and dark streaks on the inner petals from summer into autumn. Plant tuberous roots in spring in fertile, moist but well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade, leaving young plants undisturbed to build into a clump rather than dividing them early. Pull spent flowering stems from the base rather than cutting to encourage continued rebloom, and mulch the crown over winter for the first couple of seasons while the clump establishes. Its naturally tidy, low habit suits border fronts and large containers.

common_name: Princess Amina Alstroemeria (Deep Orange Peruvian Lily with Yellow Throat and Dark Markings)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots about eight inches deep in fertile, moist but well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade; Princess Amina is a selection from the Princess Lily series grown for its deep orange, dark-marked flowers.

directions: Princess Amina is an upright, bushy, clump-forming member of the Princess Lily series, bearing open clusters of funnel-shaped, deep orange flowers with yellow throats and dark markings from early summer to mid-autumn. Plant tuberous roots about eight inches deep in late summer, autumn, or spring in fertile, moist but well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade, and leave young plants undisturbed to grow into clumps, mulching over winter for the first two years. It is well suited to borders and containers and makes a long-lasting cut flower.

common_name: Princess Ivana Alstroemeria (Rosy Pink Peruvian Lily with Burgundy-Streaked Yellow Throat)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots in spring in fertile, moist, well-drained soil in full sun or light shade, sheltered from wind; Princess Ivana is a selection from the Princess Lily series.

directions: Princess Ivana is a densely branched, tuberous member of the Princess Lily series, producing a profusion of rosy pink, two-inch flowers with a yellow throat and burgundy streaks on the inner petals from early summer into fall. Plant tuberous roots in spring in fertile, moist, well-drained soil in full sun or light shade, choosing a site sheltered from wind and avoiding dry soils. It is reliable, low-maintenance, and attracts butterflies and other pollinators while being generally ignored by deer.

common_name: Princess Sara Alstroemeria (Creamy-Yellow Peruvian Lily Splashed Pink and Flecked Crimson)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots in spring in moist but well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade; Princess Sara is a compact selection from the Princess Lily series.

directions: Princess Sara is a compact, clump-forming member of the Princess Lily series, with creamy-yellow, funnel-shaped flowers whose inner petals are splashed pink, flecked dark crimson, and marked with yellow throats, borne in open terminal clusters from summer to mid-autumn. Plant tuberous roots in spring in moist but well-drained soil of any reasonable fertility in full sun or partial shade. Leave the clump undisturbed once established and mulch over winter while young, pulling rather than cutting spent stems to prolong the bloom season.

common_name: Princess Carmina Alstroemeria (Pinkish-Red Peruvian Lily with Pale, Finely Speckled Throat)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots in spring in fertile, moist but well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade; Princess Carmina grows taller than most Princess series selections.

directions: Princess Carmina is a somewhat taller, clump-forming member of the Princess Lily series, bearing clusters of pinkish-red, funnel-shaped flowers with paler throats and fine darker speckling through summer and autumn. Plant tuberous roots in spring in fertile, moist but well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade, and leave young plants undisturbed to form clumps, applying a dry mulch for the first two winters. It is a reliable border and cut-flower selection, growing noticeably larger than most other Princess series members.

common_name: Inca Joli Alstroemeria (Deep Orange-Red Peruvian Lily with Yellow Striped Throat)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots about eight inches deep in fertile, moist but well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade; Inca Joli is a selection from the Inca series.

directions: Inca Joli is a bushy, clump-forming member of the Inca series bred for garden and cut-flower use, with dark green, lance-shaped leaves and funnel-shaped, deep orange-red flowers whose inner petals carry yellow, striped throats from early summer into autumn. Plant tuberous roots about eight inches deep in late summer, autumn, or spring in fertile, moist but well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade, leaving the clump undisturbed once established. Pull spent stems from the base rather than cutting them to prompt continued flushes of bloom.

common_name: Inca Bandit Alstroemeria (Red Peruvian Lily with Dark Whiskered Throat Markings)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Inca Bandit is a compact selection from the Inca series with long summer-to-autumn bloom.

directions: Inca Bandit is a compact herbaceous member of the Inca series, producing red flowers marked with distinctive dark, whisker-like streaks in the throat from June into November. Plant tuberous roots in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to part shade, and leave the clump undisturbed once established, mulching over winter where marginally hardy. Its compact size and long bloom window make it well suited to containers and border fronts as well as cutting.

common_name: Inca Aurelia Alstroemeria (Yellow Peruvian Lily with Speckled Center and Coral-Pink Shading)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots in spring in well-drained soil in part sun to full sun; Inca Aurelia is a compact Inca series selection noted for being hardier than most Peruvian lilies.

directions: Inca Aurelia is a compact, upright, and bushy selection from the Inca series marketed through the Proven Winners/Proven Selections line, bearing yellow blooms with speckled centers and coral-pink shading atop well-branched, green-leaved plants. It blooms from spring through autumn with a peak in early-to-mid summer and is noted for being hardier than most Alstroemeria. Plant tuberous roots in spring in well-drained soil with part sun to full sun exposure and average water, leaving clumps undisturbed once established; it is an easy-care choice for borders, containers, cutting, and specimen use.

common_name: Little Miss Davina Alstroemeria (Dwarf Soft Pink and Yellow Peruvian Lily)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots shallowly in spring in rich, well-drained soil in full sun; Little Miss Davina is a dwarf selection from the Little Miss series bred by Robert Goemans.

directions: Little Miss Davina is a dwarf member of the Little Miss series, a group of compact Alstroemeria hybridized by Robert Goemans in Sussex, England. It produces six-inch spikes of soft pink flowers whose inner petals are lightly spotted with maroon over a yellow throat, surrounded by soft pink outer tepals, in late spring and early summer. Plant tuberous roots shallowly in spring in rich, well-drained soil in full sun, and pull rather than cut spent stems to encourage rebloom; its dwarf habit suits patio containers and border edges.

common_name: Little Miss Tara Alstroemeria (Dwarf Reddish-Pink Peruvian Lily with Black-Striped Yellow Base)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots shallowly in spring in rich, well-drained soil in full sun; Little Miss Tara is the tallest selection in the dwarf Little Miss series.

directions: Little Miss Tara is the tallest member of the dwarf Little Miss series, a group of compact Alstroemeria hybridized by Robert Goemans in Sussex, England, bearing eight-to-twelve-inch spikes of black-striped reddish-pink flowers with a yellow base in late spring and early summer. Plant tuberous roots shallowly in spring in rich, well-drained soil in full sun, leaving the shallow, fibrous crown undisturbed once established. Pull spent flowering stems from the base rather than deadheading with shears to prompt further flushes of bloom.

common_name: Little Miss Sophie Alstroemeria (Dwarf White and Pink Bicolor Peruvian Lily)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots shallowly in spring in rich, well-drained soil in full sun; Little Miss Sophie is a dwarf selection from the Little Miss series.

directions: Little Miss Sophie is a dwarf member of the Little Miss series, a group of compact Alstroemeria hybridized by Robert Goemans in Sussex, England, carrying six-inch spikes of large, open-structured bicolor flowers whose outer tepals are white with a broad pink central band, the inner petals similarly marked with maroon spotting toward a yellow base, in late spring and early summer. Plant tuberous roots shallowly in spring in rich, well-drained soil in full sun, and pull entire spent stems from the base to encourage continued rebloom.

common_name: Inticancha Paraiso Alstroemeria (Deep Velvety Purple Peruvian Lily with Flecked Centers)

planting.note: Plant tuberous roots shallowly in spring in fertile, moist but well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade; Inticancha Paraiso is a compact, long-blooming selection from the Inticancha series.

directions: Inticancha Paraiso is a clump-forming, deciduous member of the ultra-compact Inticancha series, grown for its deep, velvety purple, funnel-shaped flowers with distinctive flecked central markings, produced over a long season from June into November. Plant tuberous roots shallowly in spring in fertile, moist but well-drained soil in full sun or partial shade; the plant forms a neat, well-branched, bushy mound well suited to pots and front border positions. Pull spent stems from the base to prompt continued flowering.
